text:
John Tavares returned on Nov. 7 after missing more than three weeks, and the Maple Leafs brought him back in a new spot. "It's an adjustment," he said in TSN's headline about playing the wing, adding that he felt "not too bad". At 36, with 1,185 career points before this season, he is learning a new position.

The two games back were quiet: no points, four shots, then none against New Jersey, both losses. Before the injury he had 7 points in 7 games, four of them on the power play.

The worrying number is five on five. Toronto has taken just 34.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 13.5 points worse than without him. Nine games is a small sample and a position change makes it noisier still. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 79th among 401 forwards despite weak linemates, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 98th percentile at getting to the slot. We'd judge him in a month, not now.
headline: Tavares is back, and on the wing
